parsed.why: Documented state targeting of trans women: arbitrary detention, prosecution, forced 'examinations' amounting to torture, routine bribe extortion, impunity. An enforced criminal statute plus official hostility — the worst record here.

Criminalising morality statute with sporadic, complaint-driven convictions (Dec 2024, time served); no documented police targeting of trans people, but no recognition, no recourse, documented societal ostracism. A statutory lever without an enforcement campaign.

No criminalisation and a well-documented record with no anti-trans violence; resident recognition gaps mostly out of scope, but the dossier documents foreign markers clashing with the local register at the frontier, plus low social visibility.

No criminalisation, a constitutional equality guarantee, and no documented trans-specific harm; record is thin and dated, so the conservative, church-dominated local climate and unenforced guarantee read as mild but unverified.

No trans-specific offence and courts ruling for trans people, but documented harassment of visibly trans people in provincial cities and rising political hate speech with death threats; strong institutions only partly mitigate.
